Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates significant cardiomegaly and prominent pulmonary arteries, which are characteristic radiographic signs of chronic pulmonary artery hypertension. Long-standing PA hypertension causes right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation (leading to cardiomegaly) and weakens the pulmonary arterial wall, predisposing the patient to complications such as a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm.
